chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ali ibn Uqba from al-Husayn ibn Musa from Burayd and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever buys the food of a people while they are unwilling/dislike it, their flesh will be cut from him on the Day of Resurrection."
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for buying food from people who dislike the sale?
ai.summary: In the context of *al-Gharar* (uncertainty or risk) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the severity of forcing a sale upon an unwilling party, a concept distinct from but related to general uncertainty in contracts. The visceral imagery of having one's flesh cut off serves as a *karamah* (miraculous sign) or severe divine retribution, emphasizing that the seller's reluctance invalidates the spiritual validity of the transaction. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on consent (*rida*) as a core pillar of commercial justice, extending beyond mere legal validity to eschatological accountability.
